title: Pour syrup into water
hook: 100 mL of syrup meets 400 mL of water. How strong is the mix?

knows: that stirring sugar into water makes it sweet
doesNotKnow: that adding water leaves the number of sugar particles unchanged
that concentration is amount divided by the volume of the whole mixture

misconception: Adding water weakens a solution by changing the amount of the dissolved stuff, or concentration falls in proportion to the water added rather than to the total volume.
objective: The learner can explain that dilution keeps the amount of solute fixed and spreads it over more volume, so 100 mL made up to 500 mL has one fifth the concentration: 0.10 mol / 0.500 L = 0.20 mol/L.

claims.text: Amount concentration is the amount of solute divided by the volume of the solution (the whole mixture), in mol/L. On the stage, 1.0 mol/L means 1 mol of sugar in each litre.
claims.source: IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology (Gold Book), entry 'amount concentration' (c = n/V, V the volume of the mixture). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): IUPAC Gold Book A00295 (via search result summary; site not directly reachable): amount concentration = amount of constituent divided by the volume of the mixture, unit mol dm^-3 = mol/L; source Green Book 2nd ed. p. 42. Demo.tsx conc() = mol / (mixture mL / 1000), and the reveal divides by the 500 mL of mixture.

claims.text: 100 mL of 1.0 mol/L sugar syrup holds 0.10 mol of sugar.
claims.source: n = c x V = 1.0 mol/L x 0.100 L = 0.10 mol.

claims.text: Made up to 500 mL, the mixture is 0.20 mol/L, one fifth of the start; at 200, 300 and 400 mL it is 0.50, 0.33 and 0.25 mol/L.
The lesson treats volumes as adding up (100 mL + 400 mL = 500 mL); for dilute sugar solutions this is a close approximation.
claims.source: Approximation stated, not a measurement. Volume change on mixing dilute sucrose solutions is well under 1%; see CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 'Concentrative properties of aqueous solutions' (sucrose density table). A fact-checker should confirm the size of the effect at 1 mol/L.

claims.text: Each of the 20 dots stands for 0.005 mol of sugar; the dots are a model, not individual molecules.
claims.source: 0.10 mol / 20 dots = 0.005 mol per dot. Representation choice of the lesson.

claims.text: The bottom 100 mL holds 20, 10, 6 or 7, 5 and 4 dots at 100, 200, 300, 400 and 500 mL (6 on this stage's own dots at 300 mL).
claims.source: Dots are placed one per twentieth of the liquid height, so a 100 mL share of V mL holds 20 x 100/V dots (to within one): 20, 10, 6.7, 5, 4. | CLAIM FIX 2026-10-13: Was 'about 7' at 300 mL (disputed: stage seed 4242 shows 6; exact share 6.67).

recall.question: 50 mL of a 2.0 mol/L salt solution is topped up with water to 200 mL. What is the new concentration?
recall.why: The salt stays the same (0.10 mol); it now spreads over 0.200 L, four times the volume, so 2.0 / 4 = 0.50 mol/L.
